headline: The dollar firmed before Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision, gaining most against the yen, while oil eased only slightly as regional talks in Tehran ended with a pledge to keep talking.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: The dollar firmed into the close, with the dollar index up about 0.2% to 102.0, its biggest gain against the yen. Investors leaned toward the dollar before Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision, and two-year Treasury yields climbed back above 4.70%.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Since the US–Iran war began in February, high oil has kept US inflation up, and markets expect the Federal Reserve to hold rates this Wednesday and raise them in December, which supports the dollar. What changed: The dollar gained through the New York session, ending near 102.0 on the dollar index from 101.8 on Friday. Oil fell only a little, so the inflation worry behind a December hike stayed in place. The Dallas Fed's survey of Texas factories rose to 13.4 in October, against about 7 expected, but new orders slowed sharply and the prices firms pay kept rising. The two-year Treasury yield, the one most tied to Fed expectations, rose back above 4.70%; the 10-year was steady near 4.98%. What it means: Firms paying more and an economy still growing slightly above its normal pace keep the Fed leaning toward a December hike, and higher short-term yields draw money into dollars. The question to keep asking: does Fed chair Jerome Powell keep a December hike clearly on the table on Wednesday?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US durable goods orders at 7:30 AM CT and Conference Board consumer confidence at 9:00 AM CT Tuesday, then the Fed decision at 1:00 PM CT Wednesday and the press conference at 1:30 PM CT. A hold is priced at about 93%; what matters is how clearly the Fed points to December.
numbers: Dallas Fed manufacturing (Oct) 13.4 vs ~7 expected; new orders 9.3 from 30.7

scenarios.base: The dollar holds near 102 on the index into Wednesday, with a hold and a nod to December already priced.
scenarios.bull: Firm US figures on Tuesday or a Fed that plainly signals a December hike lift short-term yields and the dollar.
scenarios.bear: A Fed that sounds less sure about December, or a sharp drop in oil, trims hike bets and pulls the dollar back toward 101.5.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro slipped about 0.2% to near $1.118 as the dollar firmed in the afternoon. A better German business survey and calmer French bond markets had lifted it in the European morning, but that lift faded before Thursday's European Central Bank decision.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: France's debt, a budget fight and street protests pushed its 10-year borrowing cost above 5% last week, weighing on the euro; late Friday, Moody's kept France's credit rating at Aa3 instead of cutting it. What changed: French yields eased and the euro led the major currencies early Monday, touching about $1.122. Germany's Ifo business climate survey rose to 90.2 in October, against 90.0 expected, its sixth rise in a row, driven by firms' hopes for the months ahead. By the New York close the euro was back near $1.118, as the dollar gained across the board. What it means: The euro's own news was mildly good, so the slip says more about the dollar than about Europe. Steadier French bonds and a brighter German outlook support the case for a European Central Bank hike in December. The question to keep asking: does ECB President Christine Lagarde keep a December hike open on Thursday?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: euro-area money supply figures at 4:00 AM CT Tuesday; the French parliament's first vote on the revenue part of the budget, which had been set for Tuesday, has been postponed. The ECB decides on Thursday at 8:15 AM CT, with Lagarde's press conference at about 8:45 AM CT; a hold is expected.
numbers: EUR/USD 1.1178 (−0.2%), high ~1.122 in the European morning

scenarios.base: The euro stays near $1.12 into Thursday's ECB decision.
scenarios.bull: An ECB that keeps December clearly open, and quiet French bond markets, lift the euro back above $1.122.
scenarios.bear: A cautious ECB or a new French budget scare pushes the euro further below $1.115.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: The pound slipped about 0.2% to near $1.335 as investors avoided big bets before Chancellor John Healey's first UK Budget on Wednesday. A much better-than-expected retail survey from the Confederation of British Industry did not help it.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: A Bank of England rate hike on November 5 is all but priced because UK inflation is running hot, and on Friday the pound hit its strongest against the euro since May 2025. What changed: The CBI's retail sales balance improved to −10 in October from −55, far better than the −47 expected: sales are still falling, but at the slowest pace in about 18 months. The pound eased anyway, against both the dollar and the euro in London, and ended near $1.3346, with the euro flat near 83.8 pence by the close. What it means: The slip reflects caution before a big event, not new weakness in the economy. The Budget matters because heavier borrowing could worry bond investors, while tighter spending would cool growth and the case for more Bank of England hikes. The question to keep asking: does the Budget calm or rattle UK bond markets?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the BRC's shop price index at 7:01 PM CT tonight, then the UK Budget on Wednesday, around 7:30 AM CT. The Bank of England decides on November 5, where a hike is about 94% priced.

scenarios.base: The pound stays quiet near $1.335 until the Budget on Wednesday.
scenarios.bull: A Budget that keeps borrowing in check calms UK bonds and lets the pound recover toward $1.34.
scenarios.bear: A Budget seen as raising borrowing pushes UK bond yields up for the wrong reasons and weighs on the pound.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: The yen was the day's weakest major currency, with the dollar up about 0.4% to near ¥157.5. Calmer markets cut demand for safe havens, and higher short-term US yields widened the gap with Japan's low rates before the Bank of Japan decides on Friday.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Japan imports nearly all its energy, so high oil has weighed on the yen this year; last week a global stock wobble briefly lifted it to a one-month high, with the dollar near ¥156.1. What changed: US stocks rose and won back last week's losses, so investors had less reason to hold the yen for safety. The two-year US yield climbed back above 4.70%, and the dollar rose from about ¥156.9 on Friday to ¥157.5. Oil eased only slightly, so there was little relief for Japan's import bill. What it means: The yen still pays far less than the dollar, and that gap wins on calm days. Its support now rests on the Bank of Japan: core inflation is back above the bank's 2% goal, and a clear signal of a December hike on Friday would help it. The question to keep asking: does the Bank of Japan say a December hike is coming?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Japan's services producer prices at 6:50 PM CT tonight, Tokyo consumer prices at 6:30 PM CT Wednesday, and the Bank of Japan decision on Friday, Japan time (late Thursday night CT), where a hold is expected.

scenarios.base: The dollar holds between ¥157 and ¥158 until the Fed and Bank of Japan decisions.
scenarios.bull: A Bank of Japan that clearly signals a December hike, or a fresh stock sell-off, pulls the dollar back toward ¥156.
scenarios.bear: A firm Fed and a cautious Bank of Japan lift the dollar above ¥158.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The franc gave up its morning gain, with the dollar up about 0.3% to near 0.828 francs by the close. Rising stocks cut demand for safe havens, and there was no Swiss news.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Swiss National Bank holds rates at zero with inflation near zero, so the franc moves mostly on global fear, and it held near a one-month high against the dollar last week. What changed: The franc was firm early on Monday, but as US stocks recovered last week's losses and the dollar gained, it slipped to about 0.828 per dollar from about 0.825 on Friday. What it means: With no Swiss data or central-bank news, the franc is following the global mood: calmer markets take away some of its safe-haven support. The question to keep asking: does a calmer Middle East keep easing demand for safe places to park money?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the UBS survey of Swiss economic expectations at 4:00 AM CT Wednesday, and the KOF economic barometer on Friday. The Swiss National Bank's next decision is December 10.

scenarios.base: The dollar stays near 0.83 francs while markets wait for the Fed.
scenarios.bull: A flare-up in the Middle East or a stock sell-off pushes the dollar back below 0.82 francs.
scenarios.bear: Rising stocks and a firm Fed lift the dollar further above 0.83 francs.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Australian dollar eased about 0.3% to near 70.2 US cents as the US dollar firmed. Australia's third-quarter inflation figures, out at 7:30 PM CT Tuesday, will likely decide whether the central bank raises rates next week.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised rates four times this year to 4.60%, and markets see a November 3 hike as close to an even bet, which has kept the Aussie near its strongest levels of the year. What changed: Nothing new from Australia today. The Aussie slipped from about 70.4 cents on Friday as the US dollar gained in the afternoon, and stayed just under 70.2 cents. What it means: The move came from the US side. The Aussie rests on Tuesday night's inflation figures: a hot reading makes a November hike likely and supports it; a soft one pushes the hike out and leaves it exposed. The question to keep asking: is underlying inflation still running near 1% a quarter?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Reserve Bank of Australia officials testify to a parliamentary committee at 7:15 PM CT Tuesday, then the third-quarter inflation figures at 7:30 PM CT (trimmed mean about +1.0% on the quarter expected). The bank decides on November 3.

scenarios.base: The Aussie holds near 70 cents until Tuesday night's inflation figures.
scenarios.bull: Hotter-than-expected inflation makes a November hike likely and lifts the Aussie above 70.5 cents.
scenarios.bear: Softer inflation pushes the hike out and pulls the Aussie below 70 cents.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The loonie eased slightly, with the US dollar up about 0.1% to near 1.402 Canadian, as US crude slipped to about $102. Markets still expect the Bank of Canada to raise rates on Wednesday, though TD Securities and Rabobank expect a hold.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Canadian dollar rose for seven straight days last week, to its strongest in about a month, helped by high oil and bets that the Bank of Canada hikes on October 28 because energy is pushing inflation up. What changed: US crude settled down about 1.5% at $101.76, trimming one support, and the US dollar's afternoon gains pushed it back above 1.40 Canadian. A Bank of Canada hike is still priced at about 75–80%. US tariff changes on some Canadian goods, signed Friday, take effect on October 30. What it means: Much of a hike is already in the loonie's price, so a hike alone may not lift it much, while a hold would be a real surprise. The question to keep asking: does Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem raise rates and signal more?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Bank of Canada decision and Monetary Policy Report at 8:45 AM CT Wednesday, with Macklem's press conference after; Canada's August GDP comes Friday at 7:30 AM CT.

scenarios.base: The loonie stays near 1.40 per US dollar into Wednesday's decision.
scenarios.bull: A hike with a signal of more pushes the US dollar toward 1.39 Canadian.
scenarios.bear: A hold, or a further oil slide, pushes the US dollar toward 1.41 Canadian.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The kiwi fell about 0.3% to near 56.8 US cents as the US dollar firmed, a day before the Reserve Bank of New Zealand decides at 8:00 PM CT Tuesday, where a rate hike is widely expected.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: New Zealand's central bank is expected to raise its rate to 3.00% from 2.75% on October 28, because inflation, at 3.7%, is still above its target, and that expectation has supported the kiwi. What changed: Nothing new from New Zealand. The kiwi was among the dollar's biggest losers on Monday, slipping from about 57.0 cents on Friday, as investors favoured the dollar before the Fed. What it means: With a hike mostly priced, what the bank says about further hikes matters more than the move itself. The question to keep asking: does the bank signal more hikes beyond this one?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Reserve Bank of New Zealand decision at 8:00 PM CT Tuesday, then the ANZ business confidence survey at 7:00 PM CT Wednesday.

scenarios.base: A hike that is already priced leaves the kiwi near 57 cents.
scenarios.bull: A hike with a clear signal of more lifts the kiwi toward 58 cents.
scenarios.bear: A hold, or a hike framed as the last, sends the kiwi back toward 56 cents.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Brent crude settled down 0.8% at about $115.81 a barrel as envoys from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey met Iran's leaders and agreed to keep talking. Early reports of a far bigger drop, to about $110, did not hold up.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Oil has stayed high since the US–Iran war began in February, and Houthi attacks on Saudi oil sites drove Brent to a six-month high last week. What changed: The weekend passed without a US strike on Iran, and on Monday Saudi Arabia's defence minister, Pakistan's army chief and Turkey's intelligence chief met Iran's leaders in Tehran. The meeting ended with a pledge of further talks, but no deal. Yemen's Houthi rebels said they hit pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline; Saudi Arabia has not confirmed it. Brent ended near $115.81, from $116.72 on Friday, and US crude fell 1.5% to $101.76. What it means: Only a little of the war premium left the price. With no deal, oil stays high enough to keep inflation worries alive, which weighs on energy importers like Japan and the euro area. The question to keep asking: do the talks produce anything concrete, or do the attacks resume?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: any result from the regional talks with Iran, the American Petroleum Institute's weekly oil stocks at 3:30 PM CT Tuesday, and official US stocks figures at 9:30 AM CT Wednesday.
numbers: Tehran talks: pledge to keep talking, no deal

scenarios.base: Brent stays between $112 and $118 while the talks continue.
scenarios.bull: A confirmed hit on Saudi oil sites or a breakdown in the talks sends Brent above $118.
scenarios.bear: A concrete step toward a ceasefire pushes Brent toward $110.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold rose about 0.9% to near $4,033 an ounce, recovering further from last week's three-month low below $4,000. Oil easing a little helped, but expectations of a December US rate hike keep the bounce modest.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Gold fell nearly 4% last week as high oil raised fears of more inflation and more US rate hikes; gold pays no interest, so it suffers when rates rise. What changed: Gold climbed back above $4,000 and held there, ending near $4,033 from about $3,996 on Friday, even as the dollar firmed. What it means: Some buyers came back after last week's slide, but the forces that pushed it down are still in place: oil is high and a December Fed hike is still expected. The question to keep asking: what does the Federal Reserve signal about December on Wednesday?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US consumer confidence at 9:00 AM CT Tuesday, then the Fed decision at 1:00 PM CT Wednesday and the press conference at 1:30 PM CT.

scenarios.base: Gold holds just above $4,000 into Wednesday's Fed decision.
scenarios.bull: A Fed that sounds less sure about a December hike lifts gold toward $4,100.
scenarios.bear: A firm signal of a December hike pushes gold back below $4,000.

calls.text: Pound near $1.337 before Wednesday's UK Budget: with no UK data, it stays between $1.333 and $1.341 by the close; a Budget leak on borrowing moves it out of that range
calls.note: With no UK data and no Budget leak, the pound ended near $1.3346, inside the range.

calls.text: Brent near $114 after Aramco cleared its Dhahran headquarters: a Houthi hit that cuts Saudi output lifts Brent past its May highs and supports the loonie; a quiet weekend lets it ease toward $110
calls.note: Both happened in turn: Houthi attacks lifted Brent to about $117 on Friday without a confirmed cut to Saudi output, then a quiet weekend and talks in Tehran took it to about $110 by Monday.

calls.text: Canada retail sales Fri 7:30 AM CT (about +1.3% expected for August): a strong rebound lifts bets on Bank of Canada hikes beyond October 28; a miss keeps it to one
calls.note: Sales rose 1.2%, a touch under the 1.3% expected, so neither a strong beat nor a miss; Bank of Canada hike pricing for October 28 stayed near 75–80%.

calls.text: Brent near $112 after the Iran strike-plan report: a confirmed hit on Gulf oil output or a US move toward strikes pushes it above the $112.68 high and lifts the yen and franc; an official denial lets it slip toward $108 by the close
calls.note: Brent did top the high, to about $113, and the yen and franc gained, but without a confirmed hit or an official US move: the report alone and Iran's tanker claims did it.

calls.text: Euro-area consumer confidence 9:00 AM CT (about −17 expected) with France's gap over Germany at its widest since 2011: a weaker reading keeps the euro under $1.12; a steady one lets it recover
calls.note: The reading was weaker (−17.9), yet the euro recovered to about $1.1218 as US yields fell, so the bond rally outweighed the survey.

calls.text: US bond rally on war fears: if the 10-year yield stays near 5.05% into the close, the yen holds its gains near ¥157; if yields rebound on the strong claims figure, the dollar climbs back toward ¥158
calls.note: Yields did not rebound; they fell further, to about 4.95%, on a tech sell-off, and the yen extended its gains to about ¥156.85.

calls.text: US 10-year yield below 5% after the tech sell-off: if Asian and European stocks keep falling overnight, the yen pushes toward ¥156 and the dollar index slips under 101.5; a rebound in stocks lifts yields and the dollar back toward ¥157.5
calls.note: Asian stocks kept falling (Nikkei −1.3%) and the dollar dipped to about ¥156.3, but steadied near ¥156.9 by 12:40 AM CT; the dollar index held at about 101.5 rather than slipping under it.

calls.text: Euro-area flash business surveys Fri 3:00 AM CT (manufacturing ~52.7, services ~52.6 expected), hours before Moody's on France: misses keep the euro near $1.12; beats firm December ECB hike bets and lift it
calls.note: The surveys missed (euro-area composite 51.9, France back in contraction at 48.4), and the euro stayed near $1.12.

calls.text: US flash PMIs Fri 8:45 AM CT (services ~58.0 expected) and Michigan inflation expectations 9:00 AM CT: firm readings lift yields back toward 5% and steady the dollar; soft ones extend the bond rally
calls.note: The surveys were firm on prices and the Michigan inflation outlook ticked up; the 10-year yield rose back to about 5.00% and the dollar index firmed to about 101.8 on Friday.

calls.text: SNB policy summary 2:30 AM CT: worry about a strong franc keeps December cut bets alive and caps the franc; a calmer tone lets it firm
calls.note: Calmer tone: the bank dropped its stronger readiness to intervene and gave no December cut signal. The franc firmed slightly, with the dollar near 0.823, and hit a three-month high against the euro.

calls.text: Saudi departure order: widening across the Gulf or a hit on Saudi output puts Brent well above $110 and lifts the dollar and loonie; staying contained lets oil drift
calls.note: Brent did climb well above $110 (about $113 by the close), but on reports of US–Israeli strike plans and Iranian tanker claims, not a wider departure order. The loonie edged up; the dollar slipped.

calls.text: UK retail sales Fri 1:00 AM CT (−0.2% expected): a strong print lifts December hike bets and the pound; a weak one trims both
calls.note: Sales fell 0.4%, worse than expected, yet the pound reached its strongest against the euro since May 2025 on Friday as a November Bank of England hike stayed near certain.

calls.text: US jobless claims Thu 7:30 AM CT (about 200,000 expected): staying low keeps the Fed's December hike near 90%; a jump trims it and weighs on the dollar
calls.note: Claims stayed low at 194,000 (200,000 expected), near their lowest in decades. December hike bets held near 90% (CME FedWatch, Oct 21); a sharp bond rally later still pulled the dollar lower.

calls.text: Moody's review of France Fri: a downgrade widens France's gap over German yields and weighs on the euro; holding the rating eases the pressure
calls.note: Moody's held France at Aa3; French yields eased on Monday and the euro led the majors in the European morning.

calls.text: Bailey 8:00 AM CT after the 3.5% UK inflation print: backing November without promising more keeps the pound near $1.34; any opening to a December follow-up lifts it; calling energy temporary trims it
calls.note: Neither branch: Bailey gave no new signal on rates. The pound still held near $1.34 (about 1.3395 at the New York close), with December's second hike about a coin toss.

calls.text: US crude oil stocks 9:30 AM CT (industry survey: about −4.9M barrels): a big official draw keeps Brent above $110; a build lets the rebound fade
calls.note: The draw came (−3.1M barrels, far more than forecast) and Brent briefly topped $110.8, but it still faded to $108.82 at the settle after the US Treasury's tanker licence and emergency fuel loans.

calls.text: Pakistan's mediation after Iran's uranium refusal: any confirmed opening drains oil's premium and lifts the euro and yen; more warships and no talks keep Brent near $110 into the close
calls.note: No opening: Rubio called a deal extremely difficult and more US warships headed in. Brent settled at $108.82, near $110 but off its high on Washington's supply moves rather than diplomacy.

calls.text: Japan national CPI Thu 6:30 PM CT (2.1% expected): a hot print keeps the BoJ's December hike near three in four; a soft one fades it and weighs on the yen
calls.note: Neither branch: 2.1% exactly as expected (1.7% prior), though the measure that also leaves out energy jumped to 2.4%. December hike pricing held near 80%.

calls.text: US–Iran framework: confirmation by either government drains oil's risk premium and pulls US long yields lower; another denial puts Brent back toward $110
calls.note: No confirmation from either government, and no fresh denial either. Brent still climbed back toward $110 overnight, on tanker attacks spreading to the Gulf of Oman rather than on the talks.

calls.note: Neither branch: 3.1% vs 3.2% expected, core measures cooled to 1.8–1.9%. October stayed about 1 in 4 (a hold), with about one quarter-point hike priced by December; consumers' inflation expectations rose to ~3.9% in the BoC survey. Correction (Oct 20): by Monday's close swaps had jumped to ~87% for an October hike on Macklem's Saturday forecast warning; the 1-in-4 figure was stale.

calls.text: UK CPI Wed 1am CT (3.4% fc vs 3.1%): 3.5%+ starts pricing a December follow-up; soft reopens Bailey's 2027 read
calls.note: Hot branch: 3.5% vs 3.4% expected (3.1% in August), the highest in 11 months. November's hike is near certain; how much December moved was not yet verified at write.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (ANZ 3.8% y/y): hot settles the RBNZ's two-way bet toward the hike side
calls.note: Not hot: inflation came in at 3.7%, a touch soft. The hike side still settled anyway, with October 28 now about 98% priced.

calls.text: Japan CPI Fri + BoJ Oct 29-30: Ueda's 'quite close' language tested — October hike stays ~25%
calls.note: Oct 19: swaps now put an October 30 hike under 5% (BBH), below the ~25% in the call. December ~80% unchanged. October hike odds fell to about 4%, far below the ~25% in the call; Japan's inflation came in at 2.1% as expected and December (~80%) is now the meeting that matters.

calls.text: France's revenue-section budget vote Tue: a clean pass narrows the French–German spread (~141bp); a defeat or big concessions widens it and weighs on the euro
calls.note: No vote on Tuesday: it was pushed to October 27, so neither branch played out.

calls.text: UK jobs Tue 1 AM CT (earnings ~3.8% expected): sticky pay firms the BoE hike case before Wednesday's inflation; cooling pay backs Bailey's calmer view
calls.note: Sticky side won: unemployment fell to 4.7% (4.9% expected) and regular pay rose 3.7% (3.6% expected); total pay and claims were softer. Pound +0.3% to ~1.334.

calls.text: Konarak follow-through: a US confirmation or more strikes keeps oil's supply premium and lifts US yields; silence lets the morning's waiver drop resume
calls.note: No confirmation (a US official denied the strike) and no new strike overnight, yet the premium held: Brent ~$109.8 Tuesday on low Gulf flows and Iran's Hormuz claims. The waiver-driven drop did not resume.

calls.text: BoC Oct 28 with ~87% priced for a hike: a hike is mostly in the loonie already; a hold would be the surprise and hit it
NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (~3.8% y/y): near forecast keeps the ~80% hike pricing; clearly soft reopens the hold and weighs on the kiwi
calls.note: Near forecast (3.7% vs 3.8%) and hike pricing held, rising to about 98%; the kiwi dipped only briefly.
